messages:
Maya (PM): quick sync — we shipped v1.3 last night. two things: a) customers are calling out a regression in the long-runner embedding path (seen in 3 accounts), b) request for a small UX tweak on the streaming response indicator that customers keep asking for.
Ethan (Eng): looked at the trace — embedding regression looks like a change in batching behavior under long sequences, likely KV cache miss spike. reproduction is flaky but consistent on corpora with ~12k token prefixes.
Samir (QA): we have a failing test in nightly for the long-prefix embed job, PR #472 flagged it. repro steps in the test case. low flakiness locally but high on CI.
Priya (SRE): infra-wise we saw a small p95 bump for dedicated pools between 02:00–03:00 UTC aligned with the deploy. nothing saturation-y, more taily.
Zoe (Design): the streaming indicator request is just a micro change — persistent spinner -> progress bar + timestamp. customers say it helps trust during long responses. low design effort.
Maya (PM): propose we split the next 4 dev days: 60% bug (embedding regression + test hardening + canary), 40% quick UX (streaming indicator). want a conservative plan that buys us confidence before wider rollout. thoughts?
Ethan (Eng): +1 for 60/40, but we should scope the bug work: 1) quick rollback toggle to previous batching heuristic, 2) focused instrumenting + synthetic repro job, 3) patch to cache handling if root cause confirmed. the rollback toggle is highest-risk mitigation.
Samir (QA): can do a regression harness for the synthetic repro. need a couple of labeled corpora from CS — @Maya can you surface the two customer logs?
Maya (PM): on it. uploading links: https://redwood-internal.docs/bugs/emb-regression and the recordings.
Priya (SRE): recommend canary policy: 5% traffic to rollback path -> monitor p50/p95 and embedding similarity metrics for 24h. if stable, ramp. I can script the rollout with our release-bot.
release-bot: deploy-plan created: canary=5%, monitor=[p50_latency,p95_latency,embed_cos_sim], alert if embed_cos_sim drops >0.02.
Ethan (Eng): for the UX work, I'll pair with Zoe and ship a small A/B: old spinner vs progress + timestamp for 10% of sessions. should be low risk and independent.
Zoe (Design): thanks — I'll drop the assets in Figma and a brief spec doc here: https://redwood-internal.design/streaming-indicator-proposal.
Samir (QA): timeline ask: can we get the rollback toggle + canary in the next 48 hours? regression harness ready in 24h once logs are in.
Maya (PM): target: rollback toggle + canary by +48h, regression harness + test fixes by +72h, UX A/B shipped by +72h. sprint-level owners: Ethan (bug), Zoe (UX), Samir (QA), Priya (canary/runbook).
Ethan (Eng): assigning engineers: myself (lead), Noor (runtime), Javier (cache). I'll open the toggle PR and label it HOTFIX.
Samir (QA): will add test cases and a quick smoke checklist: 
```
# smoke checklist
- run repro harness
- validate embed cosine similarity vs baseline
- sanity check downstream ranking for 10 sample queries
```
Maya (PM): decision notes for roadmap: this iteration prioritizes reliability over new enhancements; small UX polish accepted where it mitigates customer confusion. we'll revisit backlog reprioritization next planning.
Priya (SRE): one ask — add a short-run synthetic job to the console that runs the long-prefix embed path every 6h so we detect regressions before customer impact. I'll prototype it today.
Ethan (Eng): 👍. also adding a tiny optimization: if the repro shows KV cache pressure, we can fall back to shorter-batch streaming for sequences >8k tokens until stable. low-effort switch.
Maya (PM): thanks team. next check-in in this thread after canary rollout. if anyone hits blockers ping me directly. :pray:
